zh_summary: @scottmelker reports Bitcoin mining software firm Luxor hacked: attackers steal 0.243 $BTC in rewards from miners by compromising management software using AI and redirecting mining work; miners paid electricity but hacker collected rewards; novel attack surface for crypto software.
en_summary: @scottmelker reports Bitcoin mining software firm Luxor hacked: attackers steal 0.243 $BTC in rewards from miners by compromising management software using AI and redirecting mining work; miners paid electricity but hacker collected rewards; novel attack surface for crypto software.
text:
Bitcoin mining software firm Luxor hacked: attackers steal 0.243 $BTC in rewards from miners

"In case you're wondering, what Luxor does is they make software that lets Bitcoin miners manage their machines. So it's not doing the mining, it's the software that does the management."

"Attackers were able to compromise that software, apparently using AI, and changed where the machines sent their mining work. So the miners kept paying for the electricity and doing the actual mining, but the attacker collected the Bitcoin rewards, which were sent to their wallet."

"It wasn't a huge amount, but again, another novel attack surface that nobody had seen coming for crypto-related software, and it becomes absolutely exhausting."

"So far this is only 0.243 Bitcoin. But if you're mining Bitcoin or looking at Bitcoin miners or using software that's related to it, now you have to be worried about that as well."

"The miners got the electricity bill for it, but the hacker got the direct deposit."

我最新的產業調查與研究結論：

1. 訂單能見度與出貨規劃：
受惠於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 強勁新訂單，Google TPU 出貨能見度已達 2029 年，優於 Nvidia GPU 與其他 AI ASIC（多數為 4Q27–2Q28）。

(1) 自 2028 年起，v9 將成 Google 自建算力的主力方案，v8 系列（8t／8i 或其設計變種）訂單可視為來自 OpenAI 與 Anthropic。

(2) 2028–2029 年合計需求數量：OpenAI 約 12M（聯發科設計的 8t），Anthropic 約 14M（Broadcom 設計的 8i），兩者需求均呈逐年成長趨勢。OpenAI 採買斷，Anthropic 則是租賃與買斷都有。

(3) 考量供應鏈限制，2027–2029 年較合理的 TPU 出貨估算分別為 8–9M、14–15M、16–18M。市場普遍預期 AI 資本支出於 2028 年見頂，但此規劃顯示 TPU 在 2029 年仍具出貨成長動能，關鍵在於 AI 服務龍頭 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的直接訂單。

2. v10 產品線與供應鏈調整：
v10 由原先的 Icefish 與 Merope／Bladerunner 改為 Quillfish，預計 2029 年量產，設計服務訂單由聯發科取得。

(1) Icefish 改為 v11，預計 2030 年量產，設計服務訂單同由聯發科取得。Merope 能見度較低，供應商未定，也可能取消。

(2) 聯發科將是 v9（Humufish & Triggerfish）與 v10（Quillfish）的獨家供應商，2027–2029 年占整體 TPU 供應比重分別約 45–50%、50–55%、55–60%。TPU 對其營收與利潤的貢獻預計逐年增加。

(3) 自 v9 起新款 TPU 均採 Intel EMIB-T 先進封裝。考量初期量產能力，預期至 2029 年仍以 v8 系列為 TPU 出貨主力。v8 預期將是聯發科與 Broadcom 未來數年的 TPU 事業獲利成長的主要來源，因長期累積的學習曲線效益明顯，加上雙方負責關鍵零組件與材料採購。

3/ 市場關注度與供應商展望：
近期事件有助提升並維持 Google TPU 的市場關注度，關鍵設計服務商聯發科與 Broadcom 可望成為供應鏈首要焦點。

(1) Nvidia CEO 接班的不確定性，有利 Google 與客戶洽談 2028 年後的長期規劃。OpenAI 與 Anthropic 均為 TPU 關鍵客戶，其 IPO 也有助提升並維持 TPU 關注度，而聯發科與 Broadcom 是市場最容易聯想到的供應商。

(2) 聯發科無疑是未來數年 TPU 的最大贏家，身為 v9 後的獨家設計供應商，加上供應比重與 TPU 出貨成長同時逐年提升，均有利 TPU 事業營收規模擴大。高毛利率的 8t 系列出貨能見度達 2029 年，為關鍵利潤來源。

(3) 因 Broadcom 主導 8i 設計，故毛利率更高於 8t，有利該公司利潤成長。不過，需注意的是，Broadcom 未來數年的營運重點為非 TPU 的 XPU 與 AI 網路晶片訂單，預計最快 2027 年，非 TPU

en_summary: The “overhead supply wall” above SPY is probably not a wall. Nearly half of SPY’s volume since June...
text:
🚨 THE “OVERHEAD SUPPLY WALL” ABOVE SPY IS PROBABLY NOT A WALL.

Nearly half of SPY’s volume since July traded between 761 and 773.

SPY closed Friday at 754.37.

The busiest price was 767, leaving a massive block of supposedly trapped investors above the market.

The conventional argument is simple:

Those investors will sell when SPY returns to breakeven, creating resistance and capping any rally.

It sounds logical.

The data does not support it.

We preregistered the test, built point-in-time volume profiles and studied SPY, QQQ, IWM and DIA back to 2016.

If overhead supply actually suppresses price, larger overhead volume should predict less upside.

It predicted the opposite.

Across the four index ETFs, heavier overhead supply was associated with greater 10-session upside, not less.

The result remained positive across 20, 60 and 120-session volume profiles and in both halves of the sample.

Then we isolated 24 comparable SPY setups.

Over the following 20 sessions:

Average return: +1.80%

Median return: +3.17%

Positive outcomes: 67%

Reached the overhead volume shelf: 67%

But here is the important part.

Comparable SPY pullbacks reached any price the same distance above the market roughly 76% of the time.

The volume shelf was not a special magnet.

It was not a reliable ceiling either.

It was simply another price.

This is not a buy signal. The sample is small, and the outcomes varied widely.

It is the removal of a sell signal.

The current 767 shelf is only 1.7

text:
"After an exhaustive search, NVIDIA names its next CEO: Jensen Huang." I joked about it Thursday. What it takes and where investors fit with some Fable help:

• Shareholders elect directors. Directors pick the CEO. Jensen's ~3.6% is big, not a majority.
• Pressure can flip boards fast: nearly all @OpenAI staff threatened to walk and @sama was back in days. Here, a petition that's gaining steam.
• Time is the ask from @altcap and @GavinSBaker who want a slow search with his return in play.
• Tuesday cuts both ways. The quarter was Jensen's; the $NVDA call is Kress's. Steady may helps board.
• The probes must go his way: @nvidia's review and Congress on Dec. 1 and 3.
• A special meeting takes 15% held a year. @Vanguard_Group and @BlackRock alone top that. Index funds don't typically start fights. Maybe the slide and potential future slide motivates them.
• No-cause director removal takes two-thirds of all shares. A board-backed 2025 fix got ~99% of votes cast and failed.
• Binding route: nominate a 2027 board Feb. 24 to Mar. 26. Vote likely next summer.
• What no letter fixes: a reported relationship with a direct report.

Anything this misses? 
$NVDA

en_summary: BearForce_Won is struggling with the line of thought that says Jensen should be brought back or that his exit was unjustified. Several things at play here.
text:
I’m struggling with the line of thought that says Jensen should be brought back or that his exit was unjustified. Several things at play here:

1/ Personal indiscretions. I grant fully that these are irrelevant as a general matter. 

2/ Indiscretions with subordinates. I can even get behind the idea that Jensen is a uniquely special circumstance and we should overlook it. 

3/ Indiscretions with a potential Chinese intel asset. Let’s also fully believe the recent reporting that suggests the evidence is suspect. 

4/ Jensen as the last defense against misguided export control policy and closed lab hegemony. This is where things get tricky. But even so, let’s grant that this is a potentially existentially important counter-competitive role to play and almost no one else has the stature to do it. 

5/ At worst, he had knowledge of hardware diversion to China in violation of export controls. This is where it becomes an incredibly easy decision. Regardless of what you believe about the controls (and I believe they are both against US interests and even worse, ineffective), knowingly circumventing them is an egregious violation of shareholder and public trust. It’s also illegal. 

6/ At best, he created the perception in his affair with Alice that he was vulnerable to influence by questionable partners that could be diverting hardware to China. He can’t really change this fact regardless how true the rest of it is. It’s deeply negligent and a failure of judgment. 

7/ By lying abou

text:
Brev was acquired by NVIDIA 2.5 yrs ago. Going from startup to a big company was a big change. 
Over drinks, I told Jensen:

“This is the biggest company I’ve ever worked for”

He smiled, looked at me, and replies: 

“Me too”

I survived this long at NVIDIA because Jensen made it feel like working at a startup. He understood that layers of a company, necessary for operationalizing work, also suppress information flow. It happens naturally:
• People want praise, so they highlight the work they’re doing well & hide problems 
• People want ownership, so they suppress ideas that don’t come from their org

Paul Tudor Jones: Almost Every Big Crash Has the Same Root Cause, Too Much Leverage Somewhere

If I think of some really, really big accidents, most of them have the same underlying reason, same underlying foundation, which is some too much leverage somewhere. Most of the leverage, most of the time, if I think of the big ones, were derivative inspired, either futures or options.

1987, that crash was 100% portfolio insurance, 100%. Had they had limits, which they didn't, it would have been a 10%, maybe 15% max, but that was 100% derivatives.

If I think about 1998, Long-Term Capital, big derivatives, they had a huge balance sheet with a lot of derivatives they were offsides on.

2000 was a little different. 2000 was the easiest bear market I've ever seen in my whole life. It's got so many similarities to right now in the sense that the bear market of 2001 and 2002 were a consequence of all the IPOs in 99, 2000, and then as they unlocked, you just had this never-ending cascade of selling.

text:
🚨🇺🇸 Jensen Huang envisage de revenir à la tête de Nvidia.

Quelques jours seulement après sa démission

D'après le FT, il en a discuté avec ses proches. Et ses alliés montent une « war room » de patrons de la Silicon Valley pour faire pression sur le board

Objectif : obtenir aussi le soutien de la Maison Blanche.

La campagne a pris de l'ampleur ce week-end :
→ Elon Musk et Tim Sweeney (Epic Games) soutiennent la lettre ouverte « Bring Jensen Back »
→ Des employés de Nvidia la signent publiquement
→ Brad Gerstner (Altimeter) et Gavin Baker (Atreides), deux gros actionnaires, demandent au board de garder « toutes les options sur la table », y compris son retour

« Tout ce qui compte dans la tech, hors labs d'IA, adore Jensen », résume un de ses soutiens, dans ta gueule Dario 

Mais ça coince et ça risque en être très très dur 
→ Scott Bessent, secrétaire au Trésor, réclame un « grand ménage » à la tête de Nvidia
→ Le board mène une enquête indépendante
→ Jensen n'a pas le contrôle du capital, donc il ne peut pas passer outre le board. Il n’a que 3.4 ish %
→ Rene Haas, le patron d'Arm, aurait été approché comme successeur (le board dit qu'aucun processus « formel » n'est lancé)

Le vrai sujet pour le marché, c'est la conformité des ventes de puces en Asie, qui va être scrutée de très près, certains annoncent qu’ils ont gonflés les chiffres en Asie. 

Et tout ça arrive à deux jours des résultats, mardi, avec Colette Kress en intérim et l’IPO d’Anthropic Jeudi sous un fond macro
